$comment: Repo registry (policy, no secrets): which repos the factory manages and what it is allowed to do in each. Runtime config stays in factory/config/<owner>_<repo>.json; the per-deployment supervision file with webhook secrets lives in fleet/. Four decisions are policy because their failure mode is not a crash: whether a repo may be auto-merged (autoMerge), which label makes an issue eligible for pickup (eligibilityLabel), which paths a run may change (pathAllowlist; vendor/ is protected everywhere regardless), and whether a passing test run is required before a branch may be pushed (requireVerification, default true — see research/multi-repo-factory-plan.md §5.19). Safety flags must be real booleans: Boolean("false") is true, so strings are rejected at load. See research/multi-repo-factory-plan.md §5.11.

repos.note: N3 dogfood target, enabled for LOCAL human-dispatched self-work only: there is no fleet entry and no published webhook listener, so nothing starts a factory here by itself; runs are started deliberately (gates/self-run-task.mjs) against this checkout. autoMerge is false permanently — drydock runs stop at the draft PR for a human to merge (§5.11). pathAllowlist deliberately excludes gates/ so a self-run cannot edit the oracles that judge it, and gates/probes/ is additionally protected. README.md and AGENTS.md are writable by decision E1 (2026-10-31): self-work documents itself, including its own operating rules, because the file is advisory while the enforcement points live outside the workspace — this registry and the reviewer. An AGENTS.md edit only changes future behaviour once a human merges it.
